evidence.V1: Front, three-quarter and silhouette all read as a round-headed stone arch with a capped wall; front outline is symmetric (A15 X error 0.0) and the keystone is centred.
evidence.V2: Big (wall + opening) and small (voussoirs, gold keystone, coursed jamb blocks, coping) exist, but the upper spandrel is a large blank slab occupying ~40 % of the front, and the voussoir ring is thin relative to it, so the medium tier is weak.
evidence.V3: Coursed jambs with a lighter impost block and a coping lip give some style, but the tall narrow opening under a flat blank wall reads stiff; the voussoir ring is not chunky or exaggerated.
evidence.V4: Close_springing and close_end_section studio show even chamfers on every jamb block, voussoir and the coping, catching consistent highlight lines.
evidence.V5: Close-ups clean: no pinches, seams or z-fighting at the springing or keystone; the small jog on the keystone's right edge in the flat close-up is the chamfer meeting the adjacent voussoir, not a defect; A17/A18 pass.
evidence.V6: One stone hue in three values (light impost/coping, mid wall, dark base course) plus one gold keystone accent; brick and sandstone colourways keep the structure.
evidence.V8: Single LF_VertexColor material, stone hue, gold keystone per wave-2 modular spec, kit-range chamfers; matches kit.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, Default collision (walkable), CanTouch off, MeshPart white + SmoothPlastic, grid-corner pivot; T1 tiling passes (iou 1.0).

top_fixes: Thicken the voussoir ring and let it stand proud of the wall so the arch is the dominant medium shape
Break up the blank upper spandrel (a string course, a few offset ashlar blocks or a slightly recessed panel)
Make the keystone chunkier and let it project above the voussoir line for a stronger stylised read
